questions.text: Enumerate the key contributors and risk factors for malnutrition, frailty, and sarcopenia in cirrhosis that are present in this case.
criteria: Reduced intake from palatability of low-sodium diet/early satiety
Prolonged overnight fasts/few daily meals
Micronutrient deficiencies (e.g., vitamin D, zinc)
Cirrhosis complications (ascites/HE) drive malnutrition and frailty
Systems factors (inflammation/metabolic dysregulation)
Comorbid obesity (sarcopenic obesity risk)
Physical inactivity/low baseline capacity
Environmental/organizational factors (food knowledge, food insecurity)

questions.text: Outline an immediate assessment plan to quantify malnutrition, frailty, and sarcopenia. Specify the tools/tests, how they are performed, and when to repeat them.
criteria: Use RFH-NPT at baseline to classify low/moderate/high risk
Document which RFH-NPT components are positive (e.g., weight loss, low intake, fluid overload)
Note prognostic significance of high RFH-NPT and track changes over time
Select a standardized frailty tool (e.g., LFI) and perform correctly
Plan longitudinal reassessment with same tool
Include handgrip/gait/chair stands where appropriate
Measure SMI at L3 on clinically-acquired CT when available
Avoid psoas-only indices due to misclassification risk
Use BIA phase angle as supportive metric; recognize fluid effects on lean estimates
6-minute walk test protocol documented
Short gait speed and/or chair stands documented
Handgrip measured with standardized protocol (avg of 3 trials)
Order vitamin D, thiamine, zinc, selenium (plus others per context)
Plan repletion strategy and monitoring (e.g., zinc with copper monitoring)
Estimate calories via indirect calorimetry or IBW-based equations

questions.text: Create an individualized nutrition plan (calories, protein, timing, and sodium strategy), including micronutrient management and disease-specific optimization.
criteria: Non-obese: target ≥35 kcal/kg IBW/day; obese: BMI-stratified targets
Personalize using indirect calorimetry when available
Protein 1.2–1.5 g/kg IBW/day for adults
Do not restrict protein in HE
Encourage diverse protein sources (e.g., vegetable, dairy)
Adjust upward in critical illness (up to 2.0 g/kg IBW/day)
Small, frequent meals every 3–4 hours while awake
Early breakfast and/or late-evening snack to reduce nocturnal fast
Personalize snack content (protein-containing options)
Consider sodium liberalization if nutrition targets unmet due to palatability
Replete vitamin D deficiency
Replete zinc (30–50 mg elemental/day) with copper monitoring
Assess/replete thiamine; consider selenium as indicated
Document safety notes (e.g., high-dose interactions/toxicity)
Optimize portal hypertensive and HE management to support nutrition/exercise
Include registered dietician and exercise professional in plan
Escalate to supervised nutrition/exercise rehab if progressive despite plan

questions.text: Prescribe a safe, cirrhosis-appropriate exercise program using FITT principles (aerobic and resistance), including safety precautions.
criteria: Confirm control of ascites/HE/variceal prophylaxis before exercise
Aerobic: aim 150–300 min/week moderate intensity (talk test); gradual progression
Resistance: ≥2 days/week, major muscle groups, progressive overload
Tailor to frailty/sarcopenia severity; consider wearables/apps; reassess function

questions.text: Define monitoring and follow-up: what outcomes to track, how often to reassess, and triggers for escalation/referral.
criteria: Reassess at least annually (compensated) or every 8–12 weeks (decompensated/active management)
Track intake, weight/BMI/waist, SMI or phase angle, LFI, handgrip/6MWT, admissions/HE
Escalate to RD/exercise physiologist–supervised rehab; consider enteral support (avoid PEG in ascites); consider transplant referral if worsening decompensation

questions.text: List the main differential diagnoses for unintended weight loss and weakness in a patient with cirrhosis and explain how you'd differentiate them.
criteria: HCC cachexia (image/labs; tumor burden, inflammatory markers)
Hypothyroidism (TSH/free T4; reversible cause of fatigue/weight change)
Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency (steatorrhea; fecal elastase; response to enzymes)
Major depressive disorder/anorexia (screen; psychosocial contributors to intake)
